claims.claim: AWS released a free AWS Emulator that simulates AWS services on a laptop, development server, or CI pipeline, and the company says autonomous agents wrote it with no engineer-written or engineer-reviewed code.
claims.episode_span: The company says autonomous agents wrote it entirely.
claims.source_title: AWS Emulator: Open-source tool for testing AWS apps locally, built by autonomous AI agents
claims.supporting_quote: Amazon Web Services has released AWS Emulator, a free tool that simulates AWS services on a developer’s laptop, a development server or in a continuous integration (CI) pipeline. The company says autonomous AI agents wrote the tool entirely, with no code written or reviewed by its engineers.

claims.claim: Matthew Goldberg, a senior principal engineer at AWS, said the team has not written or reviewed any of the emulator code.
claims.episode_span: Our team hasn’t written or reviewed any of the code
claims.supporting_quote: Our team hasn’t written or reviewed any of the code.

claims.claim: Hundreds of agents work on the emulator simultaneously and fix thousands of issues each day, against tens of thousands of tests.
claims.episode_span: Hundreds of agents fix thousands of issues a day against a library of tens of thousands of tests
claims.source_title: AWS Emulator: Open-source tool for testing AWS apps locally, built by autonomous AI agents
claims.supporting_quote: AWS says hundreds of agents work on the code simultaneously, fixing thousands of issues each day.

claims.claim: AWS Emulator does not evaluate IAM or resource-based policies as AWS does and should not be used to test security.
claims.episode_span: it does not evaluate AWS Identity and Access Management or resource-based policies the way AWS does
claims.source_title: AWS Emulator: Open-source tool for testing AWS apps locally, built by autonomous AI agents
claims.supporting_quote: It does not evaluate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) or resource-based policies as AWS does, so it should not be used to test security.

claims.claim: Gemini is available on Apple CarPlay, does not wake by voice command, and Apple does not allow third-party wake phrases.
claims.episode_span: The driver has to tap the icon. Gemini does not wake on a voice command
claims.source_title: Google’s Gemini AI Assistant Now Works On Apple CarPlay
claims.supporting_quote: To start Gemini, the driver has to press the app icon on the car screen's app drawer or side rail—it doesn't wake up via voice commands.

claims.claim: The Mac Observer said Gemini’s CarPlay rollout began on November 11.
claims.episode_span: The Mac Observer dates the global start to November 11
claims.source_title: Google Gemini Now Available on Apple CarPlay With Hands-Free AI Features
claims.supporting_quote: The global rollout began on November 11, bringing natural voice conversations, email summaries, calendar assistance, and other AI features to drivers across all supported Gemini Live languages.

claims.claim: The Commerce Department is finalizing a rule to prevent Chinese AI firms from remotely accessing advanced AI chips via data centers abroad, expanding controls to seven more countries including Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.
claims.episode_span: The rule would expand existing semiconductor controls at the Bureau of Industry and Security to seven more countries, including Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand
claims.source_title: Commerce Department Finalizing Long-Awaited AI Remote Access Rule
claims.supporting_quote: The rule, which could be announced as soon as this month, will expand existing semiconductor-related controls from the department’s Bureau of Industry and Security and extend them to seven additional countries, including Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, in an effort to prevent remote access and chip smuggling into China, the people said.

claims.source_title: Google’s Gemini Decisions API to handle up to 1,000 questions per request
claims.supporting_quote: Google’s Gemini Decisions API to handle up to 1,000 questions per request

claims.claim: Nvidia’s board has been working with an outside firm to identify potential CEO replacements for Jensen Huang, a person familiar told Bloomberg.
claims.episode_span: Nvidia’s board has been working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for chief executive Jensen Huang
claims.source_title: Nvidia Working With Outside Firm to Identify CEO Candidates
claims.supporting_quote: Nvidia Corp.’s board has been working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who is reportedly suspected of spying for China, a person familiar with the situation said.

claims.claim: Bloomberg reported Alice Huang, described as the suspected spy at the center of the Nvidia scandal, has returned to China and is in Beijing, and Beijing has denied spying allegations.
claims.source_title: Alice Huang Resurfaces in Beijing Amid Nvidia Scandal
claims.supporting_quote: Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the scandal engulfing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, has returned to China and is in Beijing, according to Bloomberg’s exclusive reporting. The chipmaker is investigating spying allegations denied by Beijing.

claims.claim: explore.org reduced monthly streaming costs by 90 percent, or nearly $85,000 a month, and latency dropped from 90 seconds to 20 seconds on Google Cloud.
claims.episode_span: cut monthly video-streaming costs by 90 percent, nearly $85,000 a month
claims.supporting_quote: explore.org has reduced its monthly streaming costs by 90%, or nearly $85k each month. It also improved its streaming speed; latency dropped from 90 seconds to just 20 seconds, giving volunteer camera operators near real-time feedback.
